title: Challenge — PostgreSQL Internals & Concurrency
description: Harder follow-up: isolation anomalies, MVCC maintenance, the planner, indexing strategy, and locking. Assumes the fundamentals deck.

questions.prompt: Two transactions each read an overlapping set, then update disjoint rows, together breaking an invariant neither saw violated. This anomaly — and the PostgreSQL level that prevents it — are:
questions.explanation: Write skew slips past snapshot isolation (REPEATABLE READ); only SERIALIZABLE (SSI) detects the dangerous read/write dependency and aborts one transaction.

questions.prompt: Autovacuum's 'freeze' work exists primarily to prevent:
questions.explanation: XIDs are 32-bit and cyclic; freezing marks old tuples as permanently visible so the counter can wrap without rows appearing to come from the future.

questions.prompt: An index-only scan can skip heap fetches only when:

options: The table has no primary key
The query runs in a read-only transaction
The visibility map marks the page all-visible and the index has every needed column
work_mem is large enough to sort the result

questions.explanation: Without all-visible pages Postgres must visit the heap to check tuple visibility, defeating the index-only optimization.

questions.prompt: In EXPLAIN ANALYZE, a large gap between estimated rows and actual rows most often points to:
questions.explanation: The planner estimates from pg_statistic; stale stats (run ANALYZE) or correlated columns (extended statistics) cause big misestimates and bad plans.

questions.prompt: Which SQL construct computes a running total across rows without collapsing them into groups?
questions.explanation: A window function with an OVER clause (e.g. SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY ...)) keeps every row while aggregating.

questions.prompt: Given sales(day date, amount numeric), write SQL for a 7-day trailing running total of amount per day, ordered by day.

payload.exemplar:
SELECT day,
       SUM(amount) OVER (
         ORDER BY day
         ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ) AS trailing_7d
FROM sales
ORDER BY day;

questions.explanation: A framed window (ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) gives the trailing 7-row sum. Graded manually.

questions.prompt: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE acquires which lock?

options: An exclusive row-level lock on the selected rows
A shared ACCESS SHARE lock only

questions.explanation: FOR UPDATE takes exclusive row locks so concurrent FOR UPDATE / UPDATE on the same rows block until commit.

questions.prompt: Explain when a covering index (B-tree with INCLUDE columns) outperforms a plain composite index, and the cost you accept on the write path.

payload.rubric: Notes INCLUDE payloads enable index-only scans without widening the key (no extra sort/uniqueness semantics); acknowledges larger index + more write/VACUUM amplification.
